title: Pallet indexing with a latched jam fault

provenance.adaptation: Independently specified for this project; no public task was copied. The coding assistant chose the state variables, priority order and fixed scan traces, then reviewed the traces against a separate Python transition implementation.
provenance.rationale: A small conveyor indexes one pallet to an exit sensor and preserves a jam indication until a deliberate reset.
provenance.review: Assistant consistency review of initialization, simultaneous commands, retained state and recovery boundaries; independent Python oracle checked against manual expected traces. Not an industrial safety certification or external expert review.

requirements: Use states IDLE, MOVING, COMPLETE and FAULT, initially IDLE. Jam forces FAULT from any state; Belt and Complete are FALSE there. With Jam FALSE, Reset returns any state to IDLE. Without Reset, FAULT is latched. Stop aborts a non-fault cycle to IDLE. In IDLE accept Start only if AtExit is FALSE and enter MOVING. In MOVING, AtExit enters COMPLETE. COMPLETE is held until Reset or Stop; Start alone does not clear it. Belt is TRUE only in MOVING, Complete only in COMPLETE and Fault only in FAULT. Execute at most one state transition per scan.
scenario: A small conveyor indexes one pallet to an exit sensor and preserves a jam indication until a deliberate reset.
scan_semantics: At scan k, sample every input once, read retained pre-state q[k], execute one transition, and observe outputs O[k] at the end of that same scan. Updated state becomes q[k+1]. Reset the instance before each test. Step 0 executes normally; initial conditions describe pre-state, not an extra delayed scan. All timing in this task is explicitly counted in invocations, not wall time.

ltl.explanation: Jam wins over Reset and Start.
Fault requires an explicit clear operation.
A valid idle start moves the pallet.
Exit arrival stops indexing in the same scan.
Movement excludes completion and fault outputs.
A latched jam remains until a cleared-jam reset, or forever if no such reset occurs; this does not assume eventual reset.

tests.purpose: Jam priority, retained fault and safe reset
